title: Hyundai Steel Trademarks "H-ONE," a Unified H-Beam Brand Eyed for AI Data Centers
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · October 2, 2026

Hyundai Steel is preparing to launch "H-ONE," a unified H-beam brand merging its rolled (RH) and fabricated (BH) steel lines, in a move industry watchers link to the fast-growing AI data center construction market. Here is what's been disclosed so far and what remains to be confirmed at the brand's official reveal.

Company Role Evidence
Hyundai Steel
KRX: 004020		 H-beam manufacturer launching the unified "H-ONE" brand Reported: trademark registration confirmed via KIPRIS, Sept 29, 2026

What's been disclosed

  • Trademark filed: Hyundai Steel completed domestic trademark registration for "H-ONE" on September 29, 2026. Korea's Intellectual Property Service database (KIPRIS) lists the mark across 55 designated product categories, including H-beams, steel building frames, and semi-processed steel materials.
  • Brand structure: H-ONE is designed to unify two existing product lines — rolled H-beams (RH), made as a single continuous piece, and fabricated H-beams (BH), which are built up to allow custom large-scale or non-standard cross-sections for project-specific use.
  • Reveal timeline: An industry town hall to unveil the brand is tentatively set for around October 7, 2026, with fuller product details expected around October 14.
  • Existing premium line: Hyundai Steel already markets a premium construction H-beam brand, "H-CORE," spanning roughly 173 products, making H-ONE a broader umbrella rather than a replacement.

Why AI data centers are the likely target

Hyundai Steel has been building toward the AI data center (AIDC) construction segment for several months. In March 2026 the company set up a "Next-Generation Power Infrastructure Sales Expansion Task Force," and in August it signed a partnership with Han Mi Global for construction-project collaboration. That same month, the company said it planned an "AIDC-specialized solution brand" pairing specialty steel materials with engineering consulting. Two products already developed under that push — "ExtraH," a premium BH-beam rated to handle up to five times the load of standard beams, and "CustomH," a customizable BH-beam — are widely expected to be folded into the H-ONE lineup. (Reported)

What's still unconfirmed

Hyundai Steel has not yet held the official brand unveiling, so pricing, the full H-ONE product list, and how directly the brand will be marketed toward AI data center construction have not been confirmed by the company. The October 7 town hall and October 14 detail reveal are both described as tentative in current reporting. (Reported)

Quick FAQ

Is H-ONE an entirely new product, or a rebrand?
Based on current reporting, it's a unifying brand for Hyundai Steel's existing rolled (RH) and fabricated (BH) H-beam lines, not a single new physical product.

Does this replace Hyundai Steel's H-CORE brand?
No confirmation of that yet. H-CORE, with about 173 products, is reported as a separate existing premium line; H-ONE appears to be a broader brand umbrella.

What's the connection to AI data centers?
Hyundai Steel has spent 2026 building AIDC-specific sales infrastructure and partnerships, and has developed heavy-load BH-beam products (ExtraH, CustomH) that analysts expect to sit under the new H-ONE brand, though the company has not officially confirmed this positioning.
